title: The Map That Made One Street Seem Loudest
title_ja: 一つの通りだけが騒がしく見えた地図
fact_notes: 市と学校の活動・測定データは架空。本文・日本語訳・問題は独自制作。

sentences.en: A city science club builds a digital map showing noise levels along different streets near several schools.
sentences.ja: 市の科学クラブは複数の学校近くの通りごとの騒音の大きさを示すデジタル地図を作ります。

sentences.en: Students collect readings with a sound-measuring device and mark each observation on a shared map.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは音を測る機器で数値を集め、各観察を共有地図に記します。

sentences.en: Their first map shows one neighborhood as consistently louder than the surrounding areas.
sentences.ja: 最初の地図では一つの地区が周囲よりいつも騒がしいように見えます。

sentences.en: However, the teacher notices that most measurements there were recorded immediately after school, when buses were arriving.
sentences.ja: しかし教師はその地区の測定の多くがバスの到着する放課後すぐに記録されていたと気づきます。

sentences.en: Other streets were measured earlier in the morning when fewer vehicles were using the road.
sentences.ja: ほかの通りは車の少ない朝の早い時間に測られていました。

sentences.en: The students question whether their map reflects permanent differences between neighborhoods or simply different times of observation.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは地図が地区間の恒常的な違いを示すのか観察時刻の違いを示すだけなのか問い直します。

sentences.en: The club decides to revise its study before displaying the map as a reliable picture of the city.
sentences.ja: クラブは都市の信頼できる姿として地図を示す前に調査を見直すと決めます。

sentences.en: Noise measurements depend on the conditions under which they are taken, including the place, time, and activity nearby.
sentences.ja: 騒音の測定値は場所、時刻、近くの活動を含め測定時の条件に左右されます。

sentences.en: For example, a road may be quiet during a school lesson but busy when families travel home in the evening.
sentences.ja: 例えば道路は授業中は静かでも夕方に家族が帰宅する時間には混むかもしれません。

sentences.en: The students learn that a single reading cannot describe every hour of a street's typical day.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは一つの数値では通りの一日のあらゆる時間を説明できないと学びます。

sentences.en: They also recognize that different devices or measuring procedures could produce results that are difficult to compare.
sentences.ja: 異なる機器や測定手順では比較しにくい結果が出る可能性も認識します。

sentences.en: Their teacher asks them to record the method and conditions along with every number on the map.
sentences.ja: 教師は地図のすべての数字とともに方法と条件を記録するよう求めます。

sentences.en: A measurement becomes more useful when another observer can understand when, where, and how it was collected.
sentences.ja: 別の観察者がいつどこでどう集めたか理解できると測定値はさらに役立ちます。

sentences.en: The club prepares a simple procedure so students can follow similar steps during the next round.
sentences.ja: クラブは次の測定でも同様の手順を踏めるよう簡単な方法を準備します。

sentences.en: For the second study, the club collects observations at several agreed times instead of recording every street only once.
sentences.ja: 二度目の調査では各通りを一回だけ測るのでなく合意した複数の時刻に観察します。

sentences.en: Instead of pretending that weather and traffic have no influence, students write notes about nearby conditions.
sentences.ja: 天候や交通が影響しないふりをせず近くの条件をメモします。

sentences.en: They compare readings from the same street at different times before making claims about differences across neighborhoods.
sentences.ja: 地区間の差を主張する前に同じ通りの異なる時刻の数値を比較します。

sentences.en: Some streets show large changes, while others appear more similar from one observation period to another.
sentences.ja: 大きく変化する通りもあれば観察時間が変わっても似た数値の通りもあります。

sentences.en: These findings make the map more complicated but also prevent the students from treating a temporary pattern as a permanent fact.
sentences.ja: 結果は地図を複雑にしますが一時的な傾向を恒久的な事実として扱うことを防ぎます。

sentences.en: The club does not claim that a few observations are sufficient to understand every possible source of noise.
sentences.ja: クラブは数回の観察で騒音のすべての原因を理解するのに十分とは主張しません。

sentences.en: Its goal is to show how careful sampling can improve a question that originally appeared simple.
sentences.ja: 目標は慎重なサンプリングがもともと単純に見えた問いをどう改善するか示すことです。

sentences.en: The students then consider how the public might interpret a map with strong colors showing quieter and louder areas.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは静かな場所と騒がしい場所を強い色で示す地図を一般の人々がどう解釈するか考えます。

sentences.en: A viewer could mistake the colors for a complete judgment about which neighborhood is a good place to live.
sentences.ja: 見る人は色をどの地区が住みやすいかについての完全な判断と取り違えるかもしれません。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the readings describe only particular measurements and do not evaluate every quality of a community.
sentences.ja: それでも数値が表すのは特定の測定であり地域社会のすべての質を評価するものではありません。

sentences.en: The group adds explanations showing the times of observation and the limits of the available information.
sentences.ja: グループは観察時刻と利用可能な情報の限界を示す説明を加えます。

sentences.en: They also choose colors that allow readers to compare values without suggesting that an entire area is simply good or bad.
sentences.ja: 地域全体が単純に良い悪いと示唆せず値を比較できる色も選びます。

sentences.en: Before publication, they ask other students what the map seems to communicate and whether any labels are misleading.
sentences.ja: 公開前に別の生徒へ地図が何を伝えて見えるか、誤解を招く表示がないか尋ねます。

sentences.en: The exercise reveals that responsible visualization involves not only collecting data but anticipating how an audience may misunderstand it.
sentences.ja: この活動は責任ある可視化がデータ収集だけでなく読者の誤解を予想することも含むと示します。

sentences.en: At the final presentation, the club displays its original map beside the revised version and explains why the differences matter.
sentences.ja: 最終発表でクラブは元の地図と修正版を並べ、違いが重要な理由を説明します。

sentences.en: Students describe which patterns appeared repeatedly and which observations remain uncertain or limited by their sampling method.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは繰り返し見られた傾向と、サンプリング方法によって不確かまたは限定的な観察を説明します。

sentences.en: As a result, visitors begin asking questions about measurement times rather than relying on the darkest color alone.
sentences.ja: その結果来訪者は最も濃い色だけに頼らず測定時刻について質問し始めます。

sentences.en: The students learn that a map is an argument about the world shaped by choices about what and when to measure.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは地図が何をいつ測るかの選択によって形づくられる世界についての一つの説明だと学びます。

sentences.en: A useful model does not need to answer every question, but it should make its evidence and limitations understandable.
sentences.ja: 役立つモデルはすべての問いに答える必要はありませんが証拠と限界を理解できるようにすべきです。

sentences.en: The club plans to improve its methods further rather than treating the second map as permanently correct.
sentences.ja: クラブは二枚目の地図を永久に正しいとみなさず方法をさらに改善する計画を立てます。

sentences.en: Good scientific communication leaves room for revision when better measurements become available.
sentences.ja: よい科学的な情報発信はよりよい測定が可能になれば修正する余地を残します。

questions.prompt: What issue does the teacher notice in the original map?
options: The areas were measured at different times.
The students did not use any device.
Only the quietest streets were included.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「しかし教師はその地区の測定の多くがバスの到着する放課後すぐに記録されていたと気づきます。」が正答の根拠です。

options: Whether maps should contain street names.
Whether the pattern reflects location or measurement time.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「生徒たちは地図が地区間の恒常的な違いを示すのか観察時刻の違いを示すだけなのか問い直します。」が正答の根拠です。

options: It always has the same value.
It cannot represent every hour of a street.
It is never collected by a device.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「生徒たちは一つの数値では通りの一日のあらゆる時間を説明できないと学びます。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What improves the usefulness of the measurements?
options: Measuring each street at a different time.
Recording when, where, and how they were made.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「別の観察者がいつどこでどう集めたか理解できると測定値はさらに役立ちます。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What comparison is made before comparing neighborhoods?
options: Readings from the same street at different times.
Numbers collected by different schools without methods.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「地区間の差を主張する前に同じ通りの異なる時刻の数値を比較します。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the club avoid claiming?
options: A few readings explain all sources of noise.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「クラブは数回の観察で騒音のすべての原因を理解するのに十分とは主張しません。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What risk comes with strongly colored maps?
options: The map will contain no locations.
Viewers may treat them as complete neighborhood judgments.
Viewers will always understand all caveats.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「見る人は色をどの地区が住みやすいかについての完全な判断と取り違えるかもしれません。」が正答の根拠です。

options: Anticipating possible misunderstandings as well as gathering data.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「この活動は責任ある可視化がデータ収集だけでなく読者の誤解を予想することも含むと示します。」が正答の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What do students learn about maps?
options: They reflect choices about what and when to measure.
They are independent of data collection.
They always give a complete picture.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「生徒たちは地図が何をいつ測るかの選択によって形づくられる世界についての一つの説明だと学びます。」が正答の根拠です。

options: The first attractive map should be accepted without checking.
One reading identifies a neighborhood's permanent character.
Map labels have no effect on readers.
Reliable scientific maps explain evidence and limits while remaining open to revision.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「よい科学的な情報発信はよりよい測定が可能になれば修正する余地を残します。」が正答の根拠です。
